title: Sharp Instrumental Variable Bounds for Categorical Exposures with Trusted and Untrusted Levels

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the arbitrary-cardinality affine endpoint envelope, finite endpoint-attaining response laws, trust nesting and strict separation, untrusted-refinement invariance, linear-time evaluation, and finite-sample Hoeffding whole-set coverage; the final math review passed with no findings and all cited leaves were source-attested. The package missed the field score floor because facet irredundancy was not proved, the LEAP calculation was not developed into a reproducible worked trust-sensitivity application, and the uniform Gaussian/local-tie inference rung remained open.
tldr: With a randomized binary instrument, binary outcome, and arbitrary finite categorical exposure, the maintained model is a saturated individual-level selected-exclusion response model. Trusted categories have shared arm-invariant potential outcomes, while untrusted categories have only arm-specific labels that complete factual outcomes and are not treated as interventions. The sharp pairwise-effect interval is governed by one two-diagonal capacity: each endpoint evaluates eight baseline affine pieces and exactly two pieces per trusted nuisance category, with finite laws attaining both endpoints. Trust is nested by an explicit response-law restriction map, and separate positive-cell witnesses show strict observed-law enlargement from selected trust and strict identified-set tightening from adding trust. Comparator scope is exact: Balke--Pearl is recovered literally only for a binary exposure; aggregating a wholly untrusted remainder recovers the relevant Gabriel--Sachs--Sjolander sharp projection and formula, not an identity of latent fine-exposure model classes; and arbitrary finite full trust has the Song--Guo--Chan--Richardson model M1 response image, with the pairwise interval transferring to models M2 through M5 by their equal-image theorem. Finite-sample whole-set coverage remains valid at ties and zero cells.
gap: Published closed forms cover binary treatment and selected small-support coarsenings, while the arbitrary finite categorical-IV characterization imposes exclusion at every treatment level and leaves pairwise effects to generic optimization. The selected-trust regime strictly contains observed laws excluded by that full model, yet can strictly tighten the two-target Balke--Pearl envelope on an open set.
fill: The two-diagonal transport reduction gives the sharp linear-size envelope and finite attaining response laws for this mixed-validity regime; trust updates, wholly untrusted refinements, and one-pass evaluation follow as consequences of the same formula.
